newsitem.title: USA: ConEd to restore 345 KV power line by Fri.
newsitem.headline: ConEd to restore 345 KV power line by Fri.

text.p: Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc (ConEd) expects to restore by Friday the last of six high-voltage transmission lines that were shut Wednesday by a substation fire, said company spokesman Michael Spall.
"Only one 345 KV line left. That's the one we're concentrating on," he said. "In the next 24 hours, it is our priority to repair and replace parts (to bring the line back into service)," he said.
The line is one of two 345 kilovolt (KV) cables which carry electricity from the Sprain Brook substation near Yonkers, N.Y., to a ConEd substation in Manhattan.
"(The fire) has been out totally this morning. We're doing some additional cleaning," he said, adding a third of 14,000 gallons of lubricant oil from the substation were spilled during the fire.

At the height of the Sprain Brook fire, southern New York including New York City, Westchester County and Long Island were hit by a brief power dip when electricity flowing into the area from northern New York state and Canada suddenly was reduced.

"We brought in 100 megawatt (MW) from PJM (Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland Interconnect)," Spall said, referring one of the steps ConEd took cope with curtailed power supplies in its service territory.
The utility also switched on fuel oil and natural gas-fired power plants in New York City to compensate for the shortfall.
Spall said the emergency measures would not be needed today.
He said ConEd still did not know how long it would take to remove and replace the damaged section of the Sprain Brook substation.
